entries.title: Nurse Diary, Monday
entries.text: Matron says the lamps on Ward C stay lit all night. Not for the patients, she says. For the corners. I did not ask what she meant. I am learning not to ask.

entries.title: Nurse Diary, Wednesday
entries.text: Tobias swears something stood at the end of the hall when the power dipped. Very tall. Very still. He kept the torch on it and it never moved. He says the instant he looked away it was closer.

entries.title: Nurse Diary, Friday
entries.text: Dr Vale wants the doors kept shut at night. Shut, not locked. 'Locked is a challenge,' he says. I think he is joking. He is not smiling when he says it.

entries.title: Nurse Diary, Sunday
entries.text: Something taps the ward pipes after midnight. Matron says do not answer. Mara answered. Mara is eight. She says it was only asking where the others had gone.

entries.title: Nurse Diary, Tuesday
entries.text: We hung rattle tins on the cellar door so we would hear it come up. It never came up. The tins rang anyway, from the inside, for a very long time.

entries.title: Nurse Diary, last page
entries.text: If you are reading this: the tall one is drawn to light, the deaf one to noise, and the third one learns you. Do not do the same thing twice. Do not hide in the same place twice.

entries.title: Letter, unsent
entries.text: Dear Ada, the food is cold and the nights are loud in a way I cannot describe. Not noise. The kind of loud a held breath is. I am writing this by a candle I was told never to blow out.

entries.title: Letter, torn
entries.text: ...they say the lockers are safest. Hold your breath when it comes close, they say, and only then. I held mine so long I saw colours. When I let it go the whole room heard me.

entries.title: Letter, folded small
entries.text: Ada, if they send you my things, do not wind the clock in the cellar. It is not a clock. It is a promise, and it is not ours.

entries.title: Hollis: the keys
entries.text: Brass for the pantry, bone for the study, iron for the chapel. The Archive wants all three turned, and the order does not matter, but the courage does.

entries.title: Hollis: the hounds
entries.text: The dogs stopped barking in autumn. They do not whimper either. They face the house and listen, and in the morning they have moved one step closer to the kennel door.

entries.title: Hollis: a watcher
entries.text: A figure by the east window, a candle in the sill. It kept to the lit side of the glass and I kept to the dark. I believe that is the whole rule. It cannot see what is not lit.

entries.title: Hollis: dinner
entries.text: The master set the table for six when only four of us remained. Nobody asked who the extra places were for. Somebody has been eating.

entries.title: Hollis: the door
entries.text: I have blocked this door from the inside. Mara's drawing is under the bed. If the house wants me it will have to knock like a guest. Push from in here and the planks will give. From out there, nothing will.

entries.title: Audio Log 1
entries.speaker: Dr Vale
entries.text: Recording. The cellar is the quietest room in the building. I find it difficult to work. The silence seems to be listening back, and it has begun to anticipate my sentences.

entries.title: Audio Log 4
entries.speaker: Dr Vale
entries.text: The subject learns. Last week it checked the lockers in order, left to right. This week it checks the one I used yesterday first. I must stop using the same locker. I must stop being predictable.

entries.title: Audio Log 7
entries.speaker: Dr Vale
entries.text: The clock below the stairs stopped at three-fourteen. I wound it and it ran exactly as long as I held my breath. I do not know what that means. I will not wind it again. Someone else will.

entries.title: Audio Log 9
entries.speaker: Dr Vale
entries.text: Lamps hold it off. Not forever, and not for free. A lit ward costs oil, and the hum of it draws the deaf one. Everything here costs something. That is not a flaw in the design. That is the design.

entries.title: Audio Log 12
entries.speaker: Dr Vale
entries.text: The gate needs a crank and a wheel, and both are in the dark behind us. It will be very loud. Whoever turns it should know that everything left in the building will come to listen.

entries.title: Sign: Quiet Hours
entries.text: WARD C. QUIET HOURS 9 PM TO 6 AM. Quiet hours are enforced by the building. Please walk. Please do not run. Please do not answer if you are called by name.

entries.title: Sign: Circuits
entries.text: CIRCUIT 1 - WARDS - LIVE. CIRCUIT 2 - CORRIDORS - DEAD. The generator needs two good fuses and a firm hand on the lever. Warn the house before you do.

entries.title: Sign: Cellar
entries.text: CELLAR. STAFF ONLY. DO NOT ANSWER KNOCKING FROM BELOW. Gate winch removed for safety. Crank and wheel to be kept apart, in separate rooms, by separate hands.

entries.title: Tobias: the fuses
entries.text: One fuse is in the stores, in the crate that smells of oil. The other is wherever the nurses kept the good coats. Throw the lever and the whole house hears. Stand near a door you can shut.

entries.title: Vale's ledger
entries.text: Subject notes. It does not enter a lit room if the lamp is a ward. It does not follow into a room that has been locked. It is not clever. It is patient, and patience works like cleverness if you give it enough nights.

entries.title: A child's drawing
entries.text: Crayon on card: a house, a small girl, and a very tall dark figure standing between two yellow lamps. Under it in careful letters: HE ONLY MOVES WHEN YOU DO NOT LOOK.

entries.title: A child's drawing
entries.text: A girl in a cupboard with her hands over her mouth. Beside the door, someone has drawn an enormous ear and no face at all. Under it: THE DEAF ONE HEARS EVERYTHING. BE QUIET LIKE A STONE.

entries.title: A child's drawing
entries.text: A door, drawn from the inside, with a chair under the handle. On the other side a smiling figure waits in a coat that is slightly the wrong size. Under it: IT KNOCKS LIKE PEOPLE.

entries.title: Note by the candle
entries.text: Someone searched this room before me. Whoever they were, they left the candle burning. I do not know why that comforts me. Perhaps because something that wants us dead would have blown it out.

entries.title: Tag on the clock
entries.text: STOPPED 3:14. DO NOT WIND. If you must wind it, wind it when the house is quiet, and have a door at your back. The ticking carries to every corner of the building.

entries.title: Chalk tally
entries.text: Chalk strokes in fives, three groups of them, all in a different hand. Below, one line only: THREE NIGHTS. THAT IS ALL IT ASKS. THREE NIGHTS AND THE LAMP STAYS LIT.

entries.title: Under the sheet
entries.text: The mirror is covered because it stopped showing us. It showed the room. Only the room, every night, a little emptier than the real one. This morning there was one fewer of us in it.

entries.title: Restraint log
entries.text: The straps were not to keep the patient in. They were to keep the patient from answering. That is what the doctor wrote. In the margin, in another hand: it was not the patient that answered.

entries.title: Note on the chair
entries.text: Please do not move the chair. It faces the wall because that is where it is listening. If it is facing you, you moved it, and you should leave.

entries.title: Pharmacy slip
entries.text: Requisition: bandages x6, lamp oil x4, batteries x8, tins x12 for the corridor rattles. Authorised: Matron. Remarks: 'the rattles are working too well. Fewer, please.'

entries.title: Chapel hymn sheet
entries.text: Hymn 9: 'Keep the lamp.' Verse three has been crossed out and rewritten in a trembling hand: 'Keep the lamp, and when it gutters, keep still. The dark has no eyes. It has attention.'

entries.title: Scrap of paper
entries.text: Wheel is under the bones. Crank is in the boiler nook. Gate is at the far end, past the water. I made it halfway. If you are reading this, I did not, and you should check the corners twice.
